summary: Clarifies how TRILL switches on a shared link choose which one handles traffic for each VLAN, the "Appointed Forwarder" mechanism. The goal is at most one switch handling native traffic per VLAN. It updates RFC 6325 and RFC 7177 and replaces RFC 6439.

eli5.summary: When several bus drivers share a stop, only one should pick up each group of passengers. This sets the rules for choosing which driver.

subtitle: How TRILL switches sharing a LAN decide which one handles each VLAN's traffic, and how they avoid loops while it changes.

tldr.problem: When several TRILL switches attach to one multi-access link, exactly one of them should handle native traffic for each VLAN. The original design had to fit every appointment inside a TRILL Hello, and two forwarders for one VLAN can create a loop.
tldr.mechanism: The Designated RBridge appoints Appointed Forwarders, preferably through link-scoped E-L1CS FS-LSPs and otherwise through Hellos. An inhibition mechanism with timers stops native frames while the situation settles, and optional Hello reduction and Port-Shutdown messages speed things up.
tldr.outcome: RFC 8139 obsoletes RFC 6439 and updates RFC 6325 and RFC 7177, and it requires all TRILL switches to support E-L1CS.

today: RFC 8139 is a Proposed Standard that obsoletes RFC 6439 and updates RFC 6325 and RFC 7177. The unit metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it.

sections.title: Introduction and Scope
sections.content:
TRILL switches, also called RBridges, can attach to multi-access LAN links that also carry end stations. When several TRILL switches attach to one link, native traffic is handled by a subset called Appointed Forwarders, with the intent that native traffic in each VLAN be handled by at most one switch. One switch can be Appointed Forwarder for many VLANs.

This document frees the mechanism from the limit imposed by the original requirement that all appointments fit within a TRILL Hello PDU. It does this by requiring support of link-scoped FS-LSPs and allowing appointments to be sent in them. It also adds optional features: detecting inconsistent VLAN-to-FGL mappings, faster notification of ports going down, and less need for inhibition.

It replaces RFC 6439, and the optimizations are orthogonal and optional. The mechanism is irrelevant on point-to-point IS-IS links and on links where all TRILL switch ports are trunk ports, and it does not affect adjacency formation, DRB election, MTU matching or the forwarding of TRILL Data frames. Where this document conflicts with RFC 6325 or RFC 7177, this document prevails.
sections.eli5: Several grown-ups wait at the same door, but only one should let in the kids of each class. This document explains how they pick who does what and how to avoid two of them doing the same job.

sections.title: Appointing Forwarders
sections.content:
The Appointed Forwarder for VLAN-x is the TRILL switch that ingresses native frames from the link and egresses them to the link in that VLAN. By default the DRB (Designated RBridge) is in charge of native traffic for all VLANs on the link. It may act as forwarder itself and may appoint others. If it loses adjacency to a switch it appointed, it SHOULD immediately appoint another forwarder or take over.

Two forwarders for the same VLAN at the same time could form a loop where frames are not protected by a TRILL hop count. This is why appointment is paired with the inhibition mechanism.

The DRB has two ways to appoint. Mechanism A puts appointments in E-L1CS FS-LSPs, which legacy RBridges do not see. Mechanism B puts Appointed Forwarders sub-TLVs in a TRILL Hello sent on the Designated VLAN, and every appointment the DRB sends in Hellos must be in that Hello, since anything omitted is implicitly revoked. The E-L1CS method is RECOMMENDED; Hello appointments are needed only to appoint legacy RBridges.

Each RBridge keeps an E-L1CS LSDB and a Hello appointment database, and counts itself forwarder for a VLAN if either says so. A receiver only accepts Hello appointments from the port that won the DRB election, and only for VLANs enabled on the port where the Hello arrived. A DRB change makes non-DRB switches drop their Hello appointments, and a new DRB ignores earlier appointment information.
sections.eli5: One boss (the DRB) hands out jobs. The boss can write the list in a big notebook that everyone can read, or squeeze a short list onto a small sticky note. The notebook is better.

sections.title: Limits, Overload and VLAN Mapping
sections.content:
If appointments must go in Hellos because legacy RBridges are present, space is limited. Assuming no more than 1,000 bytes are available, the RFC estimates that appointments for 83 RBridges would fit, so the limit only bites on links with 84 or more RBridges. The RFC expects such links to be rare. For Hello appointments, it is RECOMMENDED that the DRB resend its appointments on the Designated VLAN at least once per its Holding Time.

Disabling VLAN-x on a port cancels that switch's forwarder status for it unless the VLAN is enabled on another of its ports on the same link. Merely enabling a VLAN does not make a switch a forwarder; it only allows it to become one.

The DRB SHOULD NOT appoint an RBridge in link-state overload, and SHOULD reassign VLANs away from one that becomes overloaded, if another switch is available.

If the DRB sees a Hello sent on VLAN-y arrive on VLAN-x, VLAN mapping is occurring inside the link. It MUST then arrange that the same TRILL switch is Appointed Forwarder for both VLANs, otherwise a multi-destination frame could loop forever.
sections.eli5: A small sticky note only holds so many names, so a very crowded door needs the notebook. A grown-up who is already overloaded should not get extra jobs, and two classes that get mixed together need the same grown-up.

sections.title: The Inhibition Mechanism
sections.content:
For every link where it can offer end-station service, a TRILL switch keeps a DRB inhibition timer, a root bridge change inhibition timer and up to 4,094 VLAN inhibition timers, one per legal VLAN ID. The DRB and root bridge change timers MUST be implemented. VLAN timers SHOULD be kept per VLAN, and at least two MUST be implemented if resources are tight, but two VLANs must not be merged if the switch is forwarder for only one.

An Appointed Forwarder is inhibited for VLAN-x if any one of three timers is unexpired: the DRB timer, the root bridge change timer or the VLAN-x timer. Timers are set in situations such as:

  • becoming DRB (set to the Holding Time of the winning port);
  • receiving a Hello that says the sender is forwarder for VLAN-x (VLAN timer set to the longer of its current value and the Hello's Holding Time);
  • enabling a VLAN on a link where it was not enabled before;
  • seeing a change of the common spanning tree root bridge (default 30 seconds, configurable from 30 down to 0 seconds).

While inhibited, a switch still handles TRILL Data and IS-IS packets. It does not output decapsulated native frames to that link, and it ignores native frames in VLAN-x from the link except for address learning. It must still say in Hellos whether it is forwarder.

Three optional optimizations shorten root-bridge-change inhibition: a change to a lower-priority root is safe, a change of priority only (same MAC address) can be ignored, and inhibition can end once Hellos arrive from all RBridges that can see the old or new root.
sections.eli5: If the grown-ups are not sure who is in charge, they all freeze for a short time and wait. Only the kids' pick-up pauses; the other work continues.

sections.title: Hello Reduction and Multiple Ports
sections.content:
If a network manager knows the bridge and port configuration within an Ethernet link, Hellos can be sent in fewer VLANs. An RBridge MUST still always attempt to send Hellos in the Designated VLAN. Because VLAN timers normally only update from Hellos in that VLAN, two extra mechanisms keep them safe. First, an RBridge MAY include in any Hello an Appointed Forwarders sub-TLV that appoints itself. Second, it MAY use the VLANs Appointed sub-TLV, which lists the VLANs it forwards for. Support is advertised by a capability bit in the PORT-TRILL-VER sub-TLV.

If these mechanisms are used, each RBridge MUST announce so that no VLAN inhibition timer improperly expires unless three or more Hellos are lost. The RFC's example is announcing all VLANs three times per Holding Time on the Designated VLAN.

A switch may have several ports on the same link. Suspended ports never ingress or egress native frames. A forwarder with several active ports may load-share however it likes, as long as a frame sent out of one port can never be ingressed on another of its own ports.
sections.eli5: To save talking, helpers can announce what they do less often, as long as they still check in often enough that nobody forgets who is responsible.

sections.title: Port-Shutdown Messages
sections.content:
Other switches normally notice a failed port only after missing a number of Hellos, which can take many seconds. A TRILL switch SHOULD therefore send a Port-Shutdown message. It is an RBridge Channel message using RBridge Channel Protocol number 0x006, and its payload is a list of the Port IDs that failed or are going down. A switch planning a shutdown SHOULD also reduce its Holding Time on the port.

For robustness, it sends a configurable number of copies a configurable interval apart. The default is two copies, which can be set to one or three, spaced 20 milliseconds apart by default. The message SHOULD use priority 7 and SHOULD NOT be marked drop eligible. If the shutdown is planned within 1 second, the switch stops sending Hellos and either sends the message to capable ports on the link or broadcasts it.

On receipt, a switch drops adjacencies to the listed ports. If it is the DRB and that removes all adjacencies to that switch, it either becomes forwarder itself or appoints a new one. No special message is needed when a port returns; sending Hellos again is enough. The messages SHOULD be secured using the RBridge Channel Header Extension, because otherwise they are a potential denial-of-service vector.
sections.eli5: Instead of waiting for a bus driver to be late, the driver shouts, "I am leaving now!", so someone else can step in quickly.

sections.title: VLAN and Label Mapping Checks and New Encodings
sections.content:
TRILL maps a VLAN ID in native traffic to a 24-bit Fine-Grained Label (FGL) in TRILL Data packets. Because the forwarder can change, all switches on a link that map VLANs to FGLs SHOULD use the same mapping, or traffic could jump from one FGL to another. Switches SHOULD advertise their mappings and SHOULD alert the operator when two disagree. The alert is delayed until the problem persists for a time that defaults to the switch's Holding Time and can be set between 0 and 2**16 - 1 seconds, where the largest value disables alerts.

The document defines four new APPsub-TLVs carried in a TRILL GENINFO TLV in E-L1CS FS-LSPs:

  • AppointmentBitmap (type 17) for appointing a switch for compact VLAN ranges;
  • AppointmentList (type 18) for scattered VLANs over a large range;
  • FGL-VLAN-Bitmap (type 19) and FGL-VLAN-Pairs (type 20) for advertising FGL-VLAN mappings.

All switches MUST support E-L1CS. E-L1CS PDUs MUST NOT exceed 1,470 bytes but longer received ones are processed normally.
sections.eli5: If two helpers use different name tags for the same class, kids get confused when the helper changes. So helpers compare lists and warn the teacher if the lists disagree.

sections.title: Security
sections.content: The document does not change the security considerations of the TRILL base protocol in Section 6 of RFC 6325. Port-Shutdown messages use the RBridge Channel facility and SHOULD be secured with the Channel Header Extension; unsecured, they are a potential denial-of-service vector. E-L1CS FS-LSPs are IS-IS PDUs and can be protected with Authentication TLVs in the same way as Hellos or other IS-IS PDUs.
sections.eli5: Anyone could shout a fake "I am leaving!" So the shout should carry a secret stamp that proves who sent it.
